documents.title: AI Guidance for Faculty
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); guidance in effect since fall 2023
documents.summary: Teaching center guidance telling faculty to set their own AI policy and put an AI statement in the syllabus, with advice on understanding tools and designing instruction. It offers three sample statements and refers unit-specific rules to department chairs.
documents.stance_why: It says 'Individual instructors should feel empowered to create policies' and supplies three sample statements (No Allowance, Allowance with Restriction, Allowance without Restriction) without picking one, so the document delegates.

units.why: The page calls itself 'a starting point' and sends readers to the Department Chair for 'Department- or College-specific policies', so it sets no university rule and lets units set their own; P85 fits better than P04 because the delegation named here is to departments and colleges.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Guidelines (graduate capstone, thesis, DNP project, dissertation)
documents.summary: Graduate School rules for AI in capstones, theses, DNP projects and dissertations: disclosure, advisor consultation, verification, a short acceptable list and a list of misuses. Units may add their own guidelines, and violations are integrity matters up to dismissal.
documents.stance_why: Acceptable use is a narrow list ('Formatting documents and citations' and visuals without data) and listed misuses are barred unless a unit allows them, which is restrict rather than permit.
